transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. How can I help you today?

Hi Doctor. Lately, I've been having a really hard time staying seated when I'm supposed to, like during work meetings or dinners. I find myself constantly getting up and walking around, and it's starting to become a real problem.
When did this restlessness start? Was it after a specific stressful event, or has it been present for most of your life, even since childhood?

No, it's not from any recent stressful event. Honestly, I've felt this inner restlessness for as long as I can remember, definitely since I was a kid under 12. Back then, I was always running around and climbing on things when I wasn't supposed to.
In addition to physical restlessness, do you also have trouble with focusing, following instructions, or waiting your turn, especially in situations that require sustained mental effort?

Yes, absolutely. I often have a really hard time following through on instructions and actually finishing my work or chores. I also find it incredibly difficult to wait my turn, whether I'm waiting in a line or trying to let others speak.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidate was Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation), but based on the patient's report of significant difficulties with both inattention (trouble following instructions, not finishing tasks) and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (restlessness, difficulty waiting turn), the presentation now meets criteria for Combined Presentation. The symptoms have been present since childhood, supporting a diagnosis of ADHD rather than an acquired or situational condition.
